scope: Source-based experiment design and elementary bounds; no new learned method or theorem established
candidate_position: Geometry supervision is an ORDINARY control for the existing decision-to-action study, not an automatically novel replacement mechanism

notions.G: predicted current object geometry keyed by stable object IDs

supervision.ordinary_geometric_auxiliary: L_A(X,A) + lambda_G * sum_i m_i L_geom(G_hat_i(X), G_recorded_i)
supervision.geometry_conditioned_control: Same labels/weights; deploy G_hat from current evidence, then A(X,G_hat); never reference G or future state injected only into this arm
supervision.actual_extracted: actual_v1/current_state_geometry.jsonl: recorded state targets only, all24 units retained, no training admission

conditional_controls: Same-source auxiliary D/direct A and self-generated D-conditioned A remain the primary identified comparison
If adding geometry targets, add identical geometric supervision and parameters to both policy arms; direct-A plus ordinary search gets equivalent total compute
Native current-state tool information must be equally accessible; never hide exact available positions/bounds from the ordinary baseline
A geometry-only head/auxiliary-label improvement does not prove the learned representation is used during decisions
Geometry reconstruction, action consequences, requirement satisfaction and professional design preference are different targets

attention_path.result: For a causal sequence [images; Gaussian summaries; user text; action], summary states cannot attend to later user text or the ungenerated action. The later action can still attend directly to images.
attention_path.consequence: An image-conditioned current-state summary is not automatically a task-conditioned future-action model, nor a mandatory bottleneck for the action. Attention-mask or equivalent architecture/source evidence is needed for a stronger claim.
attention_path.status: Architecture inference from stated token order, not an audit of unreleased Imagine3D implementation

pose_to_occupancy_bound.assumptions: One fixed rigid asset K, local point norm<=r, true/predicted translations p,p_hat; nonnegative uniform scales s,s_hat; rotations R,R_hat with relative angle delta in[0,pi]. No asset-identity change.
pose_to_occupancy_bound.proof: Pair each local point with itself. Split p-p_hat +(s-s_hat)Rv + s_hat(R-R_hat)v, use triangle inequality and ||R-R_hat||_2=2sin(delta/2); obtain both directed Hausdorff bounds.
pose_to_occupancy_bound.collision_margin: If eps_i,eps_j bound the two occupied-set errors, d(pred_i,pred_j)>eps_i+eps_j implies true sets are separated. The distance functional changes by at most eps_i+eps_j.
pose_to_occupancy_bound.limit: No eps has been calibrated or bounded for our model; mean pose loss, Gaussian covariance and photometric scores do not establish such a certificate. New asset shapes require a separate shape-error term. Bounds on source bboxes are not physical stability or function guarantees.

photometric_identifiability.result: Photometric reconstruction error alone does not uniformly bound collision/support geometry without further assumptions.
photometric_identifiability.example_assumptions: Opaque primary-ray renderer, fixed cameras/material/illumination, no indirect illumination. Changes wholly invisible from those cameras leave rendered images unchanged but can affect an unseen support/collision region.
photometric_identifiability.scope: Elementary existence example, not a claim of identical renders in our actual Cycles setup or a proof against learned priors
photometric_identifiability.actual_material_issue: Different cutaway masks and 2D overlays need explicit treatment. No claim that poses cannot be reconstructed from archived source; only the existing matrix/mask contract is incomplete.

whole_generation_test.endpoint: original full scene request, all mandatory objects and relations, editable output; unknown checks separate
